notes: Correctly treats quoted braces as plain arguments by routing every structural brace check in the dispenser and parser (NextArg, NextBlock, ArgErr, addresses, directives, doImport, directive, open/closeCurlyBrace, blockTokens) through unquoted-only helpers; it skips the reference's quoted-address HasSuffix tweak and the quoted '{}' branch adjustment, but adds thorough dispenser, parser, and adapt tests.

Quoted braces are now ignored as block delimiters at the same parser and dispenser sites as the reference, including NextArg, NextBlock, directive nesting, blockTokens and import/snippet nesting, and the patch adds solid dispenser, parser and adapt tests; it misses the reference's minor tweaks to the quoted-address `HasSuffix("{")` check and the quoted `"{}"` branch.

Fixes the reported single-module for_each case by returning every import block, but parent-over-child override still works per ConfigResource rather than per instance. A parent block importing `module.child.x["a"]` therefore silently drops the child's block for `x["b"]`, the same silent-drop class of bug, which likely explains failing 2 of 3 hidden tests; tests and the slice-aliasing cleanup are otherwise solid.

Fixes the reported case where several import blocks in one module target instances of the same for_each resource, but it still deduplicates by ConfigResource across modules. A parent import for one instance therefore silently drops a child module's import for a different instance (or for other module instances), which is the same class of silent drop the issue complains about and likely why 2 of 3 hidden tests fail; the reference dedups per resource instance at expansion instead, and the added refactoring test locks in this too-coarse override.

Fixes the root cause the same way as the reference: a bare literal in parentheses is lifted into a wrapped unary-ADD DurationExpr in both the grammar and applyUnaryOp, and the generated parser is kept in sync. The new durationLiteral helper keeps the parse-time zero, division-by-zero and modulo-by-zero checks working for `(0)`. It omits the reference's Pretty() tweak for unary plus and still lets `foo[-(5s)]` skip the parse-time positivity check (which the reference also misses). Tests are strong, though a couple of FIXME comments were left in the expected errors.

Wraps a parenthesised NumberLiteral in a Wrapped unary-ADD DurationExpr, both in paren_duration_expr and in applyUnaryOpToDurationExpr, so parentheses survive round-trip; it also adds durationLiteral unwrapping so the parse-time checks for `foo[(0)]`, `/(0)` and `%(0)` keep working (the reference does not do this), and it adds good parser, printer and promqltest coverage; however, it does not update DurationExpr.Pretty to suppress the unary '+', and the wrapper's position omits the parens and has no EndPos.
